traits.notes: The seedling has a distinct rosette of leaves at the apex. The venation is very prominent, giving the leaves a somewhat rugose appearance from a distance, although the surface itself is described as glabrous. The pink tag "TOXOST2" is present on the stem.

=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides, as seen clearly in images 1, 2, and 5)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are densely arranged in a rosette-like fashion at the apex of the stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade, not divided into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (the leaf margins are smooth and continuous without teeth)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic to obovate (the leaves are broadest above the middle and taper towards the base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (the leaf tip tapers gradually to a point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the leaf base tapers to a wedge shape where it meets the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a single midrib runs from the base to the apex, with secondary veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): prominent and pinnate (the secondary veins are clearly visible, running parallel to each other and curving towards the leaf margin)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny and glabrous (the leaf surface reflects light, indicating a smooth, hairless texture)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs are visible on the leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (the petioles appear relatively short compared to the leaf blade)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petioles appear cylindrical and rounded in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (the stem appears firm and has the characteristics of a young tree seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem surface appears smooth and without hairs)
    19. Stem color: green (the visible parts of the stem are green)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears smooth)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the base of the petiole)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling has a distinct rosette of leaves at the apex. The venation is very prominent, giving the leaves a somewhat rugose appearance from a distance, although the surface itself is described as glabrous. The pink tag "TOXOST2" is present on the stem.
